papers.title: Pest and Disease Management in Soilless Systems
papers.authors: Paramjit Singh, Kapil Kumar Sharma, Shailesh Kumar Singh
papers.abstract: The highly controlled and often monocultural environments of soilless cultivation systems, while designed to optimize plant growth, can paradoxically create an ideal incubator for pest and disease outbreaks if not managed with vigilance and foresight. The absence of soil eliminates soil-borne pathogens, but the warm temperatures, high humidity, and dense plant canopies can provide a perfect haven for insects and airborne fungal spores to thrive and multiply at an astonishing rate. In these intensive systems, a small, unnoticed infestation can escalate into a full-blown epidemic with alarming speed, threatening the economic viability of the entire operation. Therefore, pest and disease management in Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) is not a reactive practice but a foundational pillar of the entire production strategy. It requires a holistic and proactive approach that moves away from a reliance on conventional chemical pesticides, which are often ill-suited for enclosed environments and can pose risks to workers and consumers. papers.title: Evaluating the benefits and risks of biological control agents for managing hemlock woolly adelgid in North America
papers.authors: Asha Wijerathna, Chris J.K. MacQuarrie
papers.abstract: Abstract The hemlock woolly adelgid (HWA), Adelges tsugae Annand, is an invasive pest devastating hemlock ( Tsuga ) forests in eastern North America. Importation biological control efforts have involved the introduction of insect predators from Asia and western North America, where HWA is native. Releases of Coccinellid ( Sasajscymnus tsugae , Scymnus ningshanensis ) and Derodontid ( Laricobius nigrinus , L. osakensis ) beetles have provided limited control of HWA, while more recent efforts with Chamaemyiid flies ( Leucotaraxis argenticollis , Le. piniperda ) show potential but have not yet established in eastern regions. This study conducts a benefit-risk analysis using native biodiversity as the common metric to assess the ecological impacts of these biological control agents (BCAs). We calculate a benefit-risk index (BRI) to quantify the benefits and risks of introduced BCAs. In developing the BRI, we consider four categories: (1) invasive HWA populations, (2) the introduced BCA species, (3) native species benefiting from HWA suppression, and (4) native species potentially at risk from BCAs. papers.title: Functional Response and Predation Potential of Arma custos (Fabricius) Against Tuta absoluta (Meyrick)
papers.authors: Yuyang Jiang, Zhao Yan, Xiujie Li, Linli Peng, Sheng‐Yen Wu
papers.abstract: The tomato leafminer, Tuta absoluta (Meyrick) (Lepidoptera: Gelechiidae), is a globally invasive pest causing severe economic losses in tomato production. We evaluated the predatory stink bug Arma custos (Fabricius) (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) using functional-response assays, a predator-density experiment, behavioral observations, Y-tube olfactometer bioassays, and a greenhouse cage trial. Depletion-aware maximum-likelihood models supported a Type III response for adult females feeding on second-instar larvae, whereas Type II models were retained for fifth-instar nymphs and adults feeding on fourth-instar larvae. At an initial density of 40 larvae, females consumed 16.2 ± 0.2 second-instar or 17.4 ± 0.5 fourth-instar larvae within 24 h. With 40 fourth-instar larvae available per arena, increasing female density from one to five reduced per capita consumption from 17.40 ± 0.51 to 5.44 ± 0.04 larvae per day. The Hassell–Varley model provided the best fit (m = 0.725; 95% CI, 0.693–0.755). In greenhouse cages, releasing three females per cage reduced cumulative damaged leaves by 60.12% by day 15. papers.title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
papers.authors: Deepak Subedi, Bharath Mallavarapu, Pranita Patil, Abhisek Niraula, Milan Kandel
papers.source: OpenAlex / Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
papers.abstract: Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow-out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. Preharvest interventions, including biosecurity, breeder and hatchery control, vaccination, litter and water management, feed hygiene, probiotics, prebiotics, organic acids, essential oils, bacteriophages, and bacteriocins, are evaluated according to mechanism, evidence strength, and commercial relevance. Postharvest interventions, including scalding, picking, evisceration control, chilling, peroxyacetic acid application, carcass rinses, post-chill treatments, and finished-product verification, are reviewed in relation to microbial reduction and process control. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.authors: Bin Huang, Heng Jiang, Huiming Wang, Shengni Liu, Ting Xie
papers.abstract: Under climate change, shifts in the geographic distribution of medicinal plants and the mechanisms underlying their quality responses provide the scientific basis for forward-looking conservation and utilization strategies. Smilax glabra Roxb., an important medicinal and edible plant in China, is currently threatened by both habitat degradation and rising market demand, yet systematic research on the evolution of its suitable habitat and the spatial patterns of quality formation remains limited. Using 571 spatially rarefied occurrence records, this study integrated ten species distribution algorithms—including an ENMeval-optimized MaxEnt model, generalized linear models, and several machine learning methods—with environmental variables screened by Spearman correlation (with FDR correction) and variance inflation factor analysis. An ensemble forecasting framework was constructed on the Biomod2 platform to simulate habitat suitability for S. glabra under current conditions and four shared socioeconomic pathways (SSP126, SSP245, SSP370, and SSP585) for the 2050s and 2090s. papers.title: Re-emergence of the screwworm larva Cochliomyia hominivorax (Coquerel) in Mexico and its impact as a zoonosis on public health
papers.authors: Carlos Víctor Hernández Ramírez
papers.source: OpenAlex / Brazilian Journal of Animal and Environmental Research
papers.abstract: Myiasis caused by Cochliomyia hominivorax (Coquerel) the "man-eater" is a re-emerging zoonotic parasitic disease affecting the living tissues of animals and humans. Following its eradication in Mexico (1991), SENASICA confirmed its reintroduction on December 24, 2024, in Catazajá, Chiapas. As of August 18, 2026, they exist 42,871 cumulative cases and 1,880 active cases across 30 states, affecting various animal species, as well as 681 human cases across 27 states in the country. In livestock, it causes losses due to reduced production, toxemia, and secondary infections. Understanding its characteristics, epidemiology, risk factors, and impact as a zoonotic risk provides us with a clearer overview of the issues. Therefore, we conducted an analysis to facilitate a better understanding from the perspectives of both human and veterinary medicine, as managing the condition without knowledge of its counterparts in the other field would fail to yield the expected results regarding medical care and prevention. Control requires early diagnosis; delayed action will allow the fly to complete its life cycle, thereby perpetuating the species.

In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Top Enrichment Factor (TEF) of toxic elements of nickel, chromium, lead, and copper was higher than other elements. The Potential Ecological Risk (PER) index showed high and very high risk for the elements. For all elements, the Hazard Index (HI) values were higher for children than for adults. papers.title: Successful bark-beetle biocontrol. A review of the only case in history Releasing Rhizophagus grandis in Georgia, France, Britain and Türkiye against Dendroctonus micans
papers.authors: Jean‐Claude Grégoire, Hazan Alkan Akıncı, Medea Burjanadze, Hugh Evans, Nick Fielding
papers.abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. A very specific predator, Rhizophagus grandis (Coleoptera, Monotomidae), has followed its prey in its territorial expansion, with temporal and spatial lags due to long distance passive transportation of D. micans with trade, and to habitat fragmentation. When both species coexist, D. micans is very sparce and only occasionally kills trees, because the high capacity of R. grandis to locate prey even at very low densities enables it to control the pest. This very particular relationship has been exploited for biological control. Mass production and inoculative releases of R. grandis have been undertaken in four countries: Georgia since 1963, France (1978), Great Britain (1983) and Türkiye (1985). papers.title: Hi-Tech Soilless Agriculture
papers.authors: Paramjit Singh, Kapil Kumar Sharma, Shailesh Kumar Singh
papers.abstract: This book provides a comprehensive exploration of soilless agriculture, focusing on hydroponics, aeroponics, and controlled environment agriculture. It delves into plant physiology, nutrient dynamics, and water management in soilless systems, offering insights into sustainable farming practices. The manuscript also examines pest and disease management, automation, and the economic aspects of soilless farming, and: Explores the principles and practices of soilless agriculture. Covers hydroponics, aeroponics, and fogponics systems. Highlights nutrient and water management in controlled environments. Discusses pest and disease management in soilless systems. Examines automation and digital tools in agriculture. This title has been co-published with Elite Publishing House. T&F does not sell or distribute the print versions in India.

papers.authors: Daniel Sánchez-García, Xím Cerdá, Elena Angulo
papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND The Argentine ant ( Linepithema humile ) is among the world’s worst invasive species. In the Doñana Biological Reserve (Spain), it is associated with human structures that provide the mild, moist conditions it needs within the hot, dry scrubland. We evaluated a habitat-modification treatment, predicting that removing this suitable habitat would eradicate the invader locally. Over an 18-year period, we monitored ant communities at a treated and an untreated site, at different distances from the human structures, before and after treatment, and analysed how temperature and worker numbers affected encounters at baits between the Argentine ant and native ants. RESULTS Distance to the human structures shaped ant communities at both sites, but only the treated site changed after treatment. There, the Argentine ant decreased close to the human structure and almost disappeared farther from it, whereas the endemic Cataglyphis tartessica and C. floricola recovered, especially close to the structure. papers.title: Implementing Bow-tie analysis to assess the main concerns regarding biodiversity change in European Seas
papers.authors: Anita Franco, Katie Smyth, Michael Elliott
papers.abstract: Marine biodiversity is adversely affected by many human activities and their pressures. As such, there is the need for a cause-consequence-response method to objectively address the risks associated with those adverse changes. Such a method is the ISO-accredited Bow-tie technique as an objective and structured approach giving the causes, preventative control measures, mitigation and compensation measures and consequences of changes to biodiversity. Here, the Bow-tie method underpinned by the cause-consequence-response DAPSI(W)R(M) framework was used and adapted to help managers map out risks to biodiversity requiring management of the human activities and their relevant pressures, in specific case study areas (termed Broad Belt Transects, BBTs). Instead of using restrictive proprietary software, a more-flexible template framework was developed in Microsoft PowerPoint to allow a broad user base. This employed standardised lists of elements (and further adapted during the application process) allowing the development of unique, but standardised and directly comparable Bow-ties for all BBTs. papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and information needs regarding norovirus infection among parents of primary school students directly affected by outbreaks: a cross-sectional study in Hangzhou, China
papers.authors: Xiaojian Duan, Kai Song, Liangliang Huo, Jiayun Wang, Jiayun Wang
papers.abstract: Background Norovirus outbreaks are prevalent in primary schools; however, few studies have specifically examined the parents directly impacted by these events. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted between January 2025 and March 2026. Parents from seven primary schools affected by norovirus outbreaks in Hangzhou, China, were invited to complete a self-administered online questionnaire. Data were collected on sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of norovirus pathogenesis, attitudes toward prevention and control, and information needs. Results A total of 322 valid responses were obtained (response rate 82.14%). Among respondents, 83.85% reported awareness of norovirus. Attitude scores were high, with a rate of 88.22% of the maximum. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Psychological characteristics could significantly impact applications for cosmetic surgery as well as precognition and satisfaction with surgery. The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between perfectionism, early maladaptive schemas, attachment styles, and body image concern by the mediating role of self-esteem in cosmetic surgery applicants. Methods: This was a predictive correlational study. The statistical population of the study included all female applicants for cosmetic surgery referring to cosmetic surgery centers in Tehran City, Iran, in 2020. A sample size of 400 women was selected based on Klein’s model (2016). The required data were collected by Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) (1989), Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale (MPS), Young Schema Questionnaire (YSQ-S3), Adult Attachment Scale (AAS), and Body Image Concern Inventory (BICI), and analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficient and structural equations in SPSS and AMOS. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. papers.title: Friends and foes in the avocado Agroecosystem: a comprehensive review of microbial interactions and associated Mycoviruses, from pathogenesis to biocontrol
papers.authors: Mireya Navarro-Márquez, Olarewaju Omoniyi Olaoluwa, Aman Thakur, Guadalupe Gutiérrez Soto, Hafiz Muhammad Nasir Iqbal
papers.abstract: Avocado production is increasingly constrained by a complex community of fungi that can function as destructive pathogens, opportunistic colonisers, or beneficial symbionts. These interactions span the entire production chain, from soilborne root pathogens such as Phytophthora cinnamomi and Rosellinia necatrix, to vascular wilt complexes caused by Harringtonia lauricola (formerly Raffaelea lauricola) vectored by ambrosia beetles, and postharvest pathogens including Colletotrichum, Lasiodiplodia, Pestalotiopsis, and Alternaria. At the same time, the avocado agroecosystem hosts a diverse assemblage of beneficial microbes, including fungal, antagonistic bacteria, yeasts, and mycoviruses , which promote growth, enhance host immunity, and suppress disease. This review synthesises current knowledge using a “friends” and “foes” framework, positioning pathogenic and beneficial fungi as functional groups that shape avocado health. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). The human health risk was evaluated according to the US EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) standard method. The obtained data were analyzed by the Spearman correlation and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) in SPSS. papers.title: Hidden in the deadwood: Taxonomically curated barcode library reveals deep genetic divergence in Eurasian saproxylic beetles
papers.authors: Nermeen R. Amer, Tomasz Mamos, Rama Sarvani Krovi, Adrian Smolis, Tomasz Jaworski
papers.abstract: Abstract Saproxylic beetles are a highly diverse group of tree‐associated insects that play key roles in forest ecosystem functioning, comprising both rare primeval relicts and taxa of economic importance in timber production. Morphological identification of these beetles remains challenging due to high similarity among species‐rich taxa and a number of taxonomic specialists. While European DNA barcode reference databases have expanded in recent years, they remain dominated by western and northern populations, leaving Central and Eastern European taxa heavily underrepresented. Because previous studies have revealed pronounced east–west genetic divergence in several saproxylic beetle species, expanding barcode coverage in Central and Eastern Europe is highly necessary. Located within a biogeographical transition zone and harbouring some of Europe's last remnants of primeval forests, Poland represents a critical source of genetic data for these insects. papers.title: Effect of Drought Stress, Soil Salinity, P. indica, and MWCNs on Biodegradation of Diesel Oil in the Pb- and Cd-Polluted Soil Under Cultivation of Triticale Plant
papers.authors: , Amir Hossein Baghaie
papers.source: Crossref / Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Today, soil pollution with heavy metals and petroleum compounds is one of the main environmental problems. This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. In addition, plant inoculation with P. indica significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil by 12.3%. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. This reframes a persistent gap in philosophy of mind: qualia have long been debated while the physical architecture that must bound it has been neglected. papers.title: Microbiome-mediated resilience and cross-generational consequences in male Drosophila exposed to combined environmental stressors
papers.authors: Komal Maggu, Abhishek Meena, Alessio N. De Nardo, Benjamin Eggs, Sonja H. Sbilordo
papers.source: OpenAlex / Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: Climate change exposes organisms to multiple, interacting stressors, yet their joint effects on reproduction and inheritance remain poorly understood. This study investigated the interactive effects of acute heat stress and sublethal imidacloprid exposure on the reproductive success of male Drosophila melanogaster and the subsequent fitness of their offspring. We manipulated the gut microbiome of male flies (germ-free or colonized with one or five bacterial species) and subjected them to individual or combined stress. We show that combined stressors act synergistically to reduce male fitness traits, an effect that is partially buffered by higher microbiome diversity. Paternal stress exposure further reduced offspring fertility, demonstrating cross-generational fitness costs largely independent of microbial transmission. Our results underscore the gut microbiome as an important, but stress-sensitive, contributor to host resilience, and demonstrate how multi-stressor interactions can amplify reproductive failure, with broad implications for population persistence and biodiversity loss in a warming, chemically altered world.

papers.abstract: The excessive use of antibiotics in recent years has led to serious consequences such as the microbial resistance. In response to this problem, essential oils from the genus Piper have been extensively investigated for their diverse biological properties, including antimicrobial activity. This work presents the chemical composition of the essential oil (EO) of Piper brachypetiolatum and its antimicrobial and modulatory action against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli . For this purpose, the leaves of P. brachypetiolatum were subjected to hydrodistillation in a Clevenger apparatus. The essential oil yield was 0.85%, and 11 compounds were identified by gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and gas chromatography with flame ionization detection (GC-FID). The main constituents were (E)-nerolidol (24.51%) and hinesol (23.55%). The essential oil showed antimicrobial activity against resistant strains of S. aureus (CBAM 324) and E. coli (CBAM 02), with mean inhibition zones of 17 mm and 13 mm, respectively, and a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 mg/mL for both microorganisms. papers.authors: Charlie Abi Saad, Mario Masiello, Miriam Haidukowski, Raffaele Meloni, Stefania Somma
papers.abstract: Introduction The co-occurrence of Alternaria and Fusarium species on wheat represents a food safety concern due to the accumulation of their mycotoxins in grains. While fungicides are widely applied to control Fusarium Head Blight (FHB), their effects on Alternaria alternata growth and mycotoxin production remain poorly investigated. This study aimed to evaluate the activity of different fungicides, largely used to control FHB, against A. alternata both in vitro condition and in soft wheat fields under two different crop systems, minimum or conventional tillage. Materials and methods The sensitivity of A. alternata to fungicides was evaluated by mycelial growth assay. The impact of sub-lethal doses of each fungicide on conidial germination and mycotoxin production was also evaluated. papers.title: Multiple strategies and cues define baleen whale migration
papers.authors: Leena Riekkola, Xuelei Zhang, Alice Della Penna, Virginia L. Andrews-Goff, Gabriela Duran
papers.source: OpenAlex / Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: Migration is a do-or-die life-history strategy, yet factors shaping it remain poorly studied in many marine taxa, as direct observations are difficult. Building on animal migration theory, we used satellite tracking data from 21 southern right whales tagged in Aotearoa New Zealand to investigate migratory cues, timing and routes. Whales followed either a direct westward route or a longer, indirect route via higher latitudes when migrating from their wintering grounds to summer feeding grounds. Departure timing from wintering grounds was the only significant predictor of route choice, independent of sex, age class, body length or condition. Early-departing whales were more likely to follow the longer route, taking more days to migrate, yet they arrived at shared feeding grounds at similar times to whales using the direct route. These contrasting behaviours are hypothesized to reflect trade-offs between time- and energy-minimization strategies. During migration, whales may use multiple external cues to navigate, including gradients associated with ocean currents, bathymetry and magnetic inclination. papers.authors: José Arturo Molina-Mora, Flavio E. Spetale, Túlio de Lima Campos, Pedro Eduardo Romero, Lucas Inchausti
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining biosciences by enabling the analysis of complex, large-scale biological and medical data. Latin America has demonstrated remarkable potential through studies applying AI to biomedical sciences often using locally generated data and addressing regional needs. However, the integration of AI into research and healthcare in this region faces several structural challenges, including insufficient infrastructure, lack of specialized training, fragmented research systems, and continuously constrained funding. To overcome existing limitations, capacity building at the regional level is crucial. This includes developing localized AI training programs and the reinforcement of a collaborative research framework. Collaboration across institutions and countries, along with engagement from industry and government, is key to fostering an enabling environment for the responsible and effective use of AI. papers.authors: Geórgenes Hilário Cavalcante, Filipe Vieira, Rita C. Bento, Aaron Bartholomew, John A. Burt
papers.abstract: Abstract. Sir Bu Nair Island (SBN) in the central Arabian Gulf is one of the last locations in the UAE’s Gulf waters to retain extensive and well developed coral reefs, whereas many nearshore environments have experienced severe degradation following recurrent marine heatwaves. Although tides, winds and subtidal circulation are thought to influence reef-level thermal conditions at SBN, the local physical processes governing circulation and temperature variability have not previously been resolved from in situ observations. Here, we analyse a 17-month record (May 2021–October 2022) of currents, sea level, and temperature from bottom-mounted ADCPs and multi-depth temperature moorings, complemented by reanalysis of winds. Currents at SBN are strongly anisotropic and aligned along a dominant principal axis, reflecting topographic steering around the island. papers.authors: Louise D. Heitzmann, Julie Pérez, Romann Charbonnier, Marc Fichter, Xavier Hautecoeur
papers.abstract: Sex differences in social aggression are widespread across the animal kingdom, with males typic-ally displaying greater territoriality. While this dimorphism has traditionally been attributed to sex hormones, sex chromosomes can also contribute to it independently of hormonal influence. In the African pygmy mouse Mus minutoides , naturally occurring sex-reversed XY females (named X*Y due to a mutation on the X chromosome) are highly territorial in comparison to the other female genotypes present in the population (XX and XX*). However, the molecular basis of this phenotype remains unknown. Here, we evaluate molecular factors – known to correlate with aggressiveness – following a standardized behavioural assessment of aggression. papers.abstract: Natural selection favours individuals able to physiologically adjust to seasonal environmental cues, such as photoperiod, and time their reproduction accordingly. papers.abstract: The Permian-Triassic mass extinction triggered a fundamental reorganization of marine ecosystems, yet the community-level functional dynamics of early marine reptile radiations remain understudied. Here we quantify ecospace dynamics of Triassic marine reptile faunas across an approximately 20-million-year sequence in South China, integrating 10 functional traits of fossil taxa and modern ecological analogues. We identify five ecotypes defined by habitat use, foraging modes and trophic strategy. Statistical analyses reveal cumulative and incremental faunal assembly in South China in three phases: Early Triassic niche conservatism with high functional redundancy; Middle Triassic ecological radiation with expanded disparity and reduced redundancy; and late Middle to Late Triassic ecological transition and ecosystem maturation, culminating in pelagic specialization and megafaunal predation. In urban post‐agricultural grasslands, restoration often achieves reestablishment of grass species‐dominated communities, yet associated forb recovery remains limited by non‐native seedbanks and nutrient‐enriched soils. Objectives We tested whether pre‐sowing interventions that target biomass, seedbanks, and soil nutrients can improve native plant recovery, especially forbs, in a degraded urban post‐agricultural grassland. Methods We ran a randomized complete block experiment (6 blocks × 5 treatments; n = 30 plots) comparing three types of treatments: (1) biomass removal alone via glyphosate application (chemical fallow; noting that herbicide use in restoration is subject to regional regulatory requirements and practitioner preferences); (2) soil solarization (6 and 12 weeks); and (3) topsoil removal (to 7 and 14 cm depth). papers.title: Phylogeny and reassessment of the genus Tolypocladium s. lato.: Proposing a new genus, three new species and two combinations
papers.authors: Wan‐Hao Chen, Chuan-Xuan Xiong, HUI-LIN SHU, Dan Li, Qian Zeng
papers.abstract: This study presents a phylogenetic reassessment and taxonomic revision of the genus Tolypocladium s. str. in Ophiocordycipitaceae . A phylogenetic analysis based on five loci (ITS, LSU, rpb1 , rpb2 , and tef -1α) was conducted, combined with morphological characters and host associations. Traditionally, Tolypocladium species are regarded as polyphyletic, with species distributed across three families of Hypocreales : Ophiocordycipitaceae , Cordycipitaceae , and Clavicipitaceae . Consequently, we propose a new genus, Tolypocladiopsis , to accommodate Tolypocladium extinguens (in Cordycipitaceae ); describe three new species, Tolypocladium guizhouense , T. tongrenense , and T. zongqii , from Fanjing Mountain, Guizhou Province, China. Tolypocladium lignicola is accommodated in Metapochonia s. str., and we accordingly introduce M. lignicola . Our findings refine the generic delimitation of Tolypocladium , resolve long-standing taxonomic ambiguities, underscore the misleading nature of morphological convergence in hypocrealean anamorphs, and advocate for an integrative taxonomy that combines molecular phylogenetics with detailed morphological examination.
